title: Slice, and the rank bound without its unused equality case

add.label: Lemma 4.5'
add.name: Rank bound, inequality only
add.proof:
(a) Let $M$ be the matrix of all rows of all $W_c$, of rank $d := \operatorname{rank} \mathbf{W}$, and fix $u$. Choose $d$ linearly independent columns of $M$, column $0$ among them unless it is zero. Given the entries of $r$ at the other indices in $[N]$, at most one value modulo $q$ of its entries at the chosen indices solves $M r = u$. Each of the independent entries $r_1, \dots, r_N$ takes a given value modulo $q$ with probability at most $1/g$, as $g + 1 < q$; so does $r_0$ given all of them. Hence $\Pr[M r = u] \le g^{-d}$, as in Odlyzko's lemma \cite[Lemma 3.1]{NW22}.
(b) Write $v = \sum_c W_c^\top z_c$. Then $v^\top r = \sum_c z_c^\top W_c r$ is a function of $(W_c r)_c$, so it takes one value whenever $(W_c r)_c$ takes its likeliest value, and $\operatorname{gp}(v^\top) \ge \operatorname{gp}(\mathbf{W})$.
add.explain: A stack of rank d is guessed with probability at most g^(-d), and a vector of its row space is at least as easy to guess as the stack.

discharge.argument: The demand asks for the inequality gp(W) <= g^(-rank W) of part (a), so that rank >= 4 gives gp <= g^(-4) < theta, and for part (b), gp(v^T) >= gp(W) for v in the row space. Both are parts (a) and (b) of the new statement, word for word.
